value.rationale: The recent failure of Ehrhart positivity under joins raises a natural size-and-dimension boundary question. For joins of two lattice polygons—the smallest nontrivial symmetric planar pair of factors—the exact normalized-volume threshold 168 is a structural, sharp finite invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The all-parameter sign criterion and unique minimal Ehrhart-data obstruction complete the first natural planar-by-planar case, while a distinct quadratic-only example separates the two algebraic failure mechanisms. The result is specific to standard joins and makes no unsupported global dimension/minimality claim.
